title: D+ restriction of the raw Cartesian mate tower
statement: For a finite-field datum F and a finite commutative coefficient ring A, let X,V,W,Y,B,Z be finite-type F.k-schemes (the category Spaces F of [def-sf-composition-projection-data]). Let j:X -> V, b:V -> W and i:Y -> B be open immersions, with b and i quasi-compact; let q:V -> Y, p:W -> B and s:B -> Z be proper, with b p = q i a Cartesian square. For every bounded-below etale complex E on X, write N for the exact site comparison and AP for the specified pro-etale D+ tower map of [lem-sp-finite-site-tower-paste]. Let S_E be the canonical D+ inclusion isomorphism for the source word S_s J_i S_q J_j and T_E that for the output word S_(p s) J_(j b), formed by the displayed composites of the proper and open inclusion compatibilities in CartesianTower.sourceInclusion and targetInclusion. Then inclusion(AP(E)) followed by T_E equals S_E followed by the raw alpha of [def-sf-composition-projection-data] evaluated at N(E). This assertion makes no reference to the canonical compact-support compositor or to candidate comparisons.

proof.text: For the Cartesian square b p = q i, its canonical clopen lift V -> W x_B Y is an isomorphism, and the clopen projector in the intrinsic properOpenAlpha is the identity. The proper-adjunction mate, transposed again under J_i adjoint to P_i, is the inverse restriction exchange followed by the inverse open unit: open normalization makes the restricted beta the identity, and the two remaining proper unit/counit pairs cancel by the triangle identities.

The canonical site/open comparison and properOpen_site_mate identify this specific adjunct with the site-transported interchange. Naturality through the open site isomorphism at j changes the witness from N(J_j E) to J_j(N E), yielding exactly GP.

Whisker by the proper s and paste with the canonical proper and open compositors. The D+ inclusion carries these compositors to their unbounded adjunction-normalized counterparts. On expanding the three defining squares, all internal inclusion isomorphisms cancel and leave sourceInclusion and targetInclusion on the boundary.

theorem cartesianTowerRestriction
    (F : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u})
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X V W Y B Z : Spaces F}
    (j : X ⟶ V) (b : V ⟶ W) (q : V ⟶ Y) (p : W ⟶ B) (i : Y ⟶ B) (s : B ⟶ Z)
    [IsOpenImmersion ((geometry F).map j)] [IsOpenImmersion ((geometry F).map b)]
    [IsOpenImmersion ((geometry F).map i)] [QuasiCompact ((geometry F).map b)]
    [QuasiCompact ((geometry F).map i)]
    [IsProper ((geometry F).map q)] [IsProper ((geometry F).map p)]
    [IsProper ((geometry F).map s)]
    (hb : b ≫ p = q ≫ i)
    (sq : IsPullback b.hom.left q.hom.left p.hom.left i.hom.left)
    (E : FiniteSiteTower.DE A X.obj.left) :
    letI : IsOpenImmersion j.hom.left := ‹IsOpenImmersion ((geometry F).map j)›
    letI : IsOpenImmersion b.hom.left := ‹IsOpenImmersion ((geometry F).map b)›
    letI : IsOpenImmersion i.hom.left := ‹IsOpenImmersion ((geometry F).map i)›
    letI : QuasiCompact b.hom.left := ‹QuasiCompact ((geometry F).map b)›
    letI : QuasiCompact i.hom.left := ‹QuasiCompact ((geometry F).map i)›
    letI : IsProper q.hom.left := ‹IsProper ((geometry F).map q)›
    letI : IsProper p.hom.left := ‹IsProper ((geometry F).map p)›
    letI : IsProper s.hom.left := ‹IsProper ((geometry F).map s)›
    letI : IsOpenImmersion (j ≫ b).hom.left :=
      mappedCompositeOpen (geo := geometry F) j b
    letI : IsProper (p ≫ s).hom.left := mappedCompositeProper (geo := geometry F) p s
    DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.map
        (FiniteSiteTower.AP A j.hom.left b.hom.left p.hom.left s.hom.left i.hom.left
          q.hom.left sq E) ≫
      (CartesianTower.targetInclusion A (j ≫ b).hom.left (p ≫ s).hom.left
        ((FiniteSiteTower.N A X.obj.left).obj E)).hom =
    (CartesianTower.sourceInclusion A j.hom.left q.hom.left i.hom.left s.hom.left
        ((FiniteSiteTower.N A X.obj.left).obj E)).hom ≫
      (alpha (ordinary F A) j b q p i s hb).app
        ((comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X.obj.left).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          E.obj)
